newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit firms on offshore selling of dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit firms on offshore selling of dollar.

text.p: * Ringgit firms on dollar selling by offshore players
* Dollar/ringgit seen in another choppy session
* Players concerned Bank Negara will re-impose capital controls
The ringgit firmed against the dollar in early Asian trading on selling of the dollar by offshore players, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected another choppy session for dollar/ringgit as market direction was still unclear.
"Dollar's topside is likely to be capped at 2.5050 but it will not fall very much below the 2.50 level," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
He said there was talk that Bank Negara had placed orders with agent banks to sell dollar/ringgit at 2.5050.
The central bank was said to have intervened strongly in the market on Tuesday, spending an estimated $1.0 billion to help the ringgit.
Dealers said the dollar was quick to recover each time it dipped below 2.50, which suggests that shorts are willing to take quick profits.
They said the market was concerned that Bank Negara would re-impose capital controls to broaden its intervention tools.
The central bank on Wednesday warned of tough steps, including increasing interest rates, to stamp out speculation in the ringgit.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5005/10 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5033/43 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
